dataset.name: CROCUS Tipping Bucket Rain Gauge Data at Argonne National Laboratory Prairie Site
description: The Tipping Bucket Rain Gauge (TBRG) dataset contains data from both the Nova-Lynx 12 inch TBRG and the Met One 8-inch TBRG. The dataset contains one minute measurements for precipitation accumulation measured in that timeframe from both instruments. Each TBRG was equipped with heaters for all-season measurements. These data are helpful for identifying periods of drought, potential flooding, and general input for water budgets. TBRGs can be used to validate optical rain gauge data and disdrometer data collected during the CROCUS project. Data were collected at the Argonne Testbed for Multiscale Observational Science (ATMOS), a 20-acre prairie site at Argonne National Laboratory in Lemont, Illinois. The data is presented as daily NetCDF (.nc) files, each containing approximately 24 hours of observations. Files follow the naming convention of: the project (CROCUS), location (atmos), instrument name (tbrg), data level (raw, a1), and date (year, month, day). The NetCDF format can be accessed using common scientific software such as Python using xarray, netCDF4 or act-doe.
variableMeasured: EARTH SCIENCE > ATMOSPHERE > PRECIPITATION > PRECIPITATION AMOUNT

spatialCoverage.description: For the Nova Lynx TBRG, identified by variable "tbrg_rain_mm_12in_Tot', the rain gauge is installed within the rain gauge field at ATMOS in Lemont, IL. The Nova Lynx rain gauge is located outside of the alter type wind shielding that surrounds the Met One rain gauge, by approximately 0.75 meters to the east. The NovaLynx rain gauge is located approximately 65 meters south of the nearest tree line and clear from any near by obstructions.

For the Met One TBRG, identified by variable "tbrg_rain_mm_8in_Tot', the rain gauge is installed within the rain gauge field at ATMOS in Lemont, IL. The Met One rain gauge is located inside of an alter type wind shield to help block wind contamination. The alter type shielding sits approximately 5 cm taller than the lip of the rain gauge. The Met One rain gauge is located approximately 65 meters south of the nearest tree line and clear from any near by obstructions.

measurementTechnique: Both the Nova Lynx 12-inch rain gauge and the Met One 8-inch rain gauge are located within 1 m of each other and have data collected every minute. Both rain gauges are connected to a Campbell Scientific CR1000x datalogger, sampling at a 1 minute interval. The data is then the total accumulation over the 1 minute period. Both tipping bucket has a 0.01 inch or 0.254 mm amount per tip.
The Met One 8-inch rain gauge, or the 'tbrg_rain_mm_8in_Tot' in the dataset, is located within an alter type wind shielding.
The Nova Lynx 12-inch rain gauge, or 'tbrg_rain_mm_12in_Tot' is located just outside of the windshielding, to the east of the Met One rain gauge.
Between July 11, 2023 and July 16, 2023 the Met One 8-inch rain gauge (tbrg_rain_mm_8in_Tot) had a clogged. Data between that time period was removed and replaced with NaNs.
